subject: Renewal: episodic burst capacity and pricing
messages:
From: Asha Patel <asha.patel@novusretail.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@novusretail.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion — seasonal burst & price stability

Hi Logan,

We're gearing up for our next contract renewal (current term ends 2027-10-15) and wanted to get ahead of a specific ask: over the past two seasons our traffic has been highly episodic — 4–6 hour spikes for promotional windows that materially increase inference spend.

Two things are most important to Novus:
- A stable base price on our committed capacity for the next 12 months (price hold)
- Ability to absorb short-duration spikes without punitive overage rates — ideally a burst pool or credits we can draw from during peaks

I've attached a small analysis (novus_q3_spike_analysis.xlsx) showing spike days and token deltas. Can Redwood propose an approach that preserves predictability for us while keeping economics fair for you? We may also be looking at a modest commit increase (about 15%) if the burst mechanism is acceptable.

Available for a call on Wed/Thu afternoon PT.

Thanks,
Asha
Asha Patel
Head of Infrastructure & AI Ops
Novus Retail
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@novusretail.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@novusretail.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — seasonal burst & price stability

Asha — thanks for the clear note and the analysis. We can definitely design something that balances base price stability with surge protection.

High-level options that come to mind (we can flesh any of these out on a call):
1) Fixed 12-month price hold on a modest commit (you keep current per-token price for the committed amount).
2) Separate burst credit pool: prepaid credits priced at a discount to on-demand, consumed for spikes; unused credits roll forward for a short window or convert to invoice credit at term end.
3) Dynamic burst with throttled overage cap: allow bursts up to X tokens/hour at a capped overage rate tied to the commit level.

If you’re open to increasing commit by ~15% we can reduce the unit cost on committed tokens and apply a one-time burst-credit grant that scales with the uplift. I’ve looped in Kimberly and Marissa to confirm commercial constraints and approval path.

Would Thu 3:00 PM PT work for a quick alignment call?

— Logan
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Novus renewal — pricing framework thoughts

Looping in David from Finance to sanity-check margin impact. Quick notes from commercial:
- We can commit to a 12-month price hold for the committed volume if Novus signs a slightly longer notice period (30 -> 60 days) and a 15% commit uplift.
- Burst credits: propose a prepaid burst pool equal to 20% of annual committed tokens, billed upfront at 65% of on-demand. Unused credits convert to a 50% refund (credit toward invoice) at term end if usage < 50% of the pool.
- Alternatively, offer a consumption tier for bursts where overage rate is capped at 1.4x committed unit price (rather than 2.0x).

David — do we need any additional guardrails for accounting or revenue recognition?

kim
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Novus renewal — pricing framework thoughts

Kim,

Accounting notes: prepaid burst credits count as deferred revenue. The convert-to-credit at term end is fine but needs clear thresholds and a short window (we prefer conversion to an invoice credit within 60 days of term end). Also: any refundable portion should be capped (max 50% refund) and require CFO approval if > $50k.

Operational ask: add a usage dashboard view for Novus that separates committed vs burst consumption by hour-day — this keeps disputes rare. Ops can deliver this as part of the renewal onboarding (2–3 week turnaround).

— David
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@novusretail.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@novusretail.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal discussion — seasonal burst & price stability

Asha,

Thanks for the call today — I’ll summarise the proposal below so we’re aligned before I send a formal term sheet/DocuSign: 

Proposal (summary):
- Base commit: 15% uplift vs current committed tokens, 12-month price hold at current committed unit price; 60-day renewal notice.
- Burst mechanism: prepaid burst-credit pool equal to 20% of annual committed tokens (billed at 65% of on-demand rate). Unused credits convert to an invoice credit at 50% value within 60 days of term end.
- Overage cap option: if Novus prefers pay-as-you-go bursts instead of prepaid credits, overage rate capped at 1.4x committed unit price (for spikes up to 6 hours/day).
- One-time onboarding: Ops will deliver a committed vs burst usage dashboard during onboarding (2–3 week ETA).
- Approval/finance: Refunds > $50k require CFO sign-off; prepaid credits recognized as deferred revenue.

Next steps: I’ll prepare a formal counterproposal and DocuSign (link: https://docusign.net/ND-2027-0112-offer). If this summary looks right, we’ll include the prepaid credit amount for the 15% uplift and propose signature by 2027-09-10 to lock pricing.

Appreciate the constructive conversation — open to minor tweaks on the burst window (we can extend to 8 hours/day if needed).

Best,
Logan
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference

--
Attachments referenced: proposed-pricing-grid-v2.pdf (pricing table, prepaid credit math)
